body.statement: Can the second-order residual-embedding orthogonalization handle construct, for every \(\widehat m\in\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\), measurable statistics \((\widehat H^\perp_{j,b}(\widehat m):(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d)\) and data-dependent radii for which there are constants \(c_u,C_H,C_R,C_m>0\), depending only on the fixed envelope and kernels, such that uniformly over \(\mathcal M_d(\beta,L,c_0,C_0)\), every \(x\ge1\) with \(u=x+\log(2d)\le c_u n\) satisfies \[P^{\otimes n}\!\left(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)^c\ \cup\ \left\{\exists(j,b)\in\mathcal Q_d:\ |\widehat H^\perp_{j,b}(\widehat m)-H_{j,b}|>C_H\left(\sqrt{\frac{H_{j,b}u}{n}}+\frac{u}{n}+r_n^4\right)\right\}\right)\le2e^{-x}.\] On \(\mathcal G_n(x;C_m,\widehat m)\), the construction must cancel the first Gateaux derivative and the second-order diagonal bias and bound the remaining nuisance term by \[C_H\max_{r,j,b}\|\widehat m^{(r)}_{j,b}-m_{j,b}\|_{L^4(P_{C_{j,b}})}^4\le C_R\left(r_n^4+\frac{u^2}{n^2}\right),\] with \(u^2/n^2\) absorbed by the displayed \(u/n\) term. The associated null intervals must use this same \(u\)-threshold and attain joint coverage. The quantifier ranges only over \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\); no unspecified regression learner is permitted. Does such a jointly valid construction exist under this fixed protocol?
body.justification: This is the exposed uniform-nuisance kill test for one fully specified estimator class: it must establish the simultaneous \(L^4\) regression event and consume that guarantee through a fourth-order residual-embedding remainder.
body.gap: Hl\'avka, Hu\v{s}kov\'a, and Meintanis (2011) derive nuisance-aware asymptotics, Mooij et al. (2016) prove pointwise consistency for a suitable learner, and Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023) observe the tested variables; none proves the joint high-probability regression and orthogonal-HSIC expansion for the fixed four-fold local-polynomial protocol.
body.consumer: An affirmative construction for \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{LP}}\) would support honest simultaneous causal-direction inference with a reproducible nonparametric nuisance procedure.
